# iliad-111 (17.288–383) — reviewer, pass 1

Method: runbook section 2. Notes checked label by label against the line; Greek to `l` word by word; `l` to `i`; remembered English checked against the house table (Iliad and Odyssey) and against shipped units (`iliad-*.json`, `odyssey-*.json`) for each repeated word; quotation marks and speech boundaries; continuity with `iliad-110.json` (its last unit, 17.284–287, ends the boar simile with Ajax scattering the Trojans, no speech open, so nothing runs on into this part). `t` was not touched (checked: the concatenation of all `t` equals the packet lines 288–383, and every unit's `l` has as many lines as its `t`). The packet flags no scansion irregularities, so there were no hand scans to add. Severity scale: major = false statement or wrong sense in a reader-facing field; moderate = house-table violation or a note contradicting the line or its own `l`/`i`; minor = wording or precision.

## Changes made (line · field · severity · wrong · done)

1. 291 · n · moderate · ἱεμένων περ called a "genitive absolute"; there is no noun in the genitive for it to be absolute with, and iliad-095 (same line, published) calls it a genitive plural of those who wished it · now "a genitive plural participle of ἵεμαι … of those who wished to keep the evil off; they are not named".
2. 293 · n · moderate · cross-reference wrong: "Ajax … is named at 304"; he is first named at 303 (Αἴαντος) · corrected to 303.
3. 293 · n · minor · χαλκοπαρῄου called an "epic genitive"; -ου is the ordinary genitive (only -οιο is epic) · "epic" removed.
4. 295 · l, i, n · moderate · ἀκωκή rendered "point"; the table fixes ἀκωκή as "tip" (11.253, 16.323) and keeps "point" for αἰχμή (which this part has at 309) · l "spear’s tip", i "tip of the spear", note "tip".
5. 295 · i · moderate · ἱπποδάσεια given as "horse-haired" in `i`; table `i` is "thick with horsehair" (3.369, 13.614; shipped iliad-020) · i now "The helmet, thick with horsehair, split …".
6. 298 · i · moderate · μένος given as "strength" in `i`; "strength" is reserved for κράτος/σθένος and μένος is "might" in both layers (table 2.387; 5.296 λύθη … μένος τε, "his soul and his might were loosed") · i "His might was loosed on the spot".
7. 305 · n · minor · "βάλ’ at the start of 309"; βάλ’ is the second word of 309 (after τὸν) · "in 309".
8. 309 (τὸν βάλ’) · l, i, n · moderate · "collarbone" as one word; the table spells κληΐς "collar-bone" and names the one-word form as avoided (5.146, 5.579; shipped iliad-028, -032) · hyphenated in all three fields.
9. 312 · i · minor · περιβάς given as "bestrode"; the table's `i` for περιβάς (17.80) is "standing over" · "as he stood over Hippothous" (`l` "bestriding" stays; the table's `l` is "bestridden").
10. 322 · l, i · moderate · γήρασκε is an imperfect (and the note says so) but `l` read "had grown old", a pluperfect · l "was growing old"; i "who grew old as a herald beside his aged father".
11. 326 · n · major (false statement in a note) · "προσέφη is ‘addressed’ with no augment"; προσέφη = πρός + ἔφη and ἔφη is augmented (the unaugmented form is φάτο, rightly so called at 342) · clause cut to "προσέφη is ‘addressed’."
12. 357 · n · minor · `l` joins "other" and "Achaeans" ("above the other Achaeans") though Ἀχαιῶν is partitive with τινα, and the note did not say so · one clause added.
13. 360 · i, n · moderate · ἀγχιστῖνοι: `i` "in close succession" is the table's `l`; the Odyssey table (24.181, shipped odyssey-107; also iliad-004) gives `i` "one close upon another", and the note called "in close succession" "the table’s word" without naming the layer · i "the dead fell one close upon another, all together"; note says `l` keeps "in close succession" and gives the table's `i`.
14. 360, 381 · i, n · moderate · ἐπιτέλλω rendered "gave his orders"; "orders" is κελεύω's word (356, three lines earlier, "giving many orders") and the table already fixes ἐπέτελλε `i` as "gave instructions" (5.198; Nestor's own ἐπέτελλε at 11.840; shipped iliad-028) · both `i` now "gave his instructions"; both notes say "give instructions". The matching row of `new-renderings.md` (ἐπιτέλλω) was rewritten to the same, and records that it follows the table; the orchestrator may drop that row when copying, since nothing new is fixed by it.
15. 366 · n · minor · "might have been put out" is an interpretation not in the Greek (σῶν ἔμμεναι = "were safe/whole") · now "so thickly that one could not say they were still there, whole".
16. 368 · n · moderate · ἕστασαν called a pluperfect "had taken their stand", while `l` and `i` say "stood": the note contradicted its own fields · "a pluperfect with the sense of an imperfect, ‘were standing’".
17. 377 · l, i, n · moderate · ὁμάδῳ rendered "throng"; "throng" is reserved for ὅμιλος (which this part has at 293 and 364), and ὅμαδος is "uproar" (table 7.307, 9.573; shipped iliad-008, -056, -058, -076, -101) · l "in the first uproar", i "in the foremost uproar", note explains.
18. 377 · i, n · moderate · ἔφαντο is "supposed" in every shipped unit (iliad-040, -073, odyssey-019); `i` "they said … he was alive" read as an assertion · i "they supposed that he was alive"; note adjusted ("they said", here "they supposed"). `l` keeps "said".
19. about · minor · "Lycomedes and Aeneas wound men" understates (Apisaon is killed, Leiocritus falls) · "Aeneas and Lycomedes strike men down".

## Findings considered and refused

- 288 `i` omits ἤτοι ("indeed" is in `l`): the particle is weak and `i` is free; not changed.
- 305 `l` "and he, Schedius, … son" reads like an apposition to the subject although Σχεδίον is accusative: the note states it is the object of βάλ’ in 309, `l` is deliberately word-order, and `i` already uses a dash. Left.
- 328 "as I have indeed seen" for the aorist ἴδον: the English perfect for an aorist of experience has the same force here, and the note labels the aorist. Left.
- 335 note on Ἕκτόρ ("printed with its accent so"): true as stated, no false claim. Left.
- 350 `i` drops καὶ δέ ("and moreover"): `l` has it and the sentence's "and" carries it. Left.
- 364 μέμνηντο as an unaugmented pluperfect with imperfect sense: agrees with the parse already in the glossary material; an optative reading exists but nothing in the sense differs. Left (for pass 2 to look at with gloss.json).
- 366 ποτέ untranslated in `i`: it only strengthens the negation; `l` has "ever". Left.
- Repeated lines and formulae checked and unchanged: 291 (iliad-095), 301 (iliad-026), 305 (iliad-079; differs only by the necessary "Ajax" for "Teucer"), 311 (iliad-026), 314 (iliad-082), 316 (iliad-026), 319–320 (iliad-036; `i` extends the published wording with the Argive clause), 326 (iliad-106), 343 (iliad-031 and the 11.214 row), 346–347 (iliad-032), 348–349 (iliad-069), 315 (iliad-067/-082 identical), 350–351 (16.551 ἀριστεύεσκε μάχεσθαι). `l` and `i` agree with the published English in each.
- Quotation marks: speech 327–332 opens “ on 327 (with `mark`) and closes ” on 332; speech 335–340 opens “ on 335 (with `mark`) and closes ” on 340; 338 is internal. Neither speech runs in from 110 or out into 112 (333 and 342 are narrative). Correct.
- Paragraph marks (`p`) at 288, 304, 312, 319, 333, 342, 352, 366 agree with the packet's ¶ lines.
- Army names: Achaeans, Argives and Danaans follow the Greek line by line; "Greeks" appears nowhere.

(360 ἐπέτελλε, active, stays "gave his instructions" per 5.198.)
2. gloss · γήρασκε · moderate · "had grown old" is a pluperfect sense the imperfect does not have (same error pass 1 fixed in `l`) · now "was growing old".
3. gloss · ἤρικε · minor · "with no object" pinned the entry to this line · removed.
4. gloss · ὑπερδέα · moderate · "contracted from -έα" was wrong (the accusative ending -έα is not itself contracted) · now "contracted from ὑπερδεέα (Attic ὑπερδεῆ)", and "sense disputed" added to match the note.
5. gloss · ἐπιτάρροθον · minor · "one who runs to aid" asserted an etymology the note calls obscure · now "helper, ally (a rare word; the formation is obscure)".
6. gloss · πλήθεΐ · moderate · "throng" in the meaning (reserved for ὅμιλος) and "dat. of respect" (it is the dative after πεποιθότας, the thing trusted) · "multitude, great number"; "dat. after verbs of trust".
7. gloss `__broaden__` · ὁμάδῳ · moderate · known entry covers only "of manner: with a roar"; here it is a dative of place after ἐνί · broadened (old entry whole).
8. gloss `__broaden__` · ἱεμένων · minor · known entry gives only "hastening"; here ἱεμένων περ, "though eager" · broadened.
9. gloss `__broaden__` · ἔφαντο · minor · known entry says "+ fut. inf."; here it takes the accusative and a present infinitive · broadened.
10. gloss `__broaden__` · αὐτοῖο · minor · known entry covers only "after πάροιθε" and the object of τιτύσκετο; here it follows ἄγχι · broadened.
11. gloss `__broaden__` · ἠέρι · minor · known entry covers only "of means"; at the second occurrence it is a dative of cause beside πολέμῳ · broadened.
12. new-renderings.md · minor · the ἐπιτέλλω row only restated the existing table rows (4.301, 5.198) · removed.

## Checked and left

μέμνηντο (pluperfect 3 pl. with imperfect sense; the perfect optative would be μεμνῇατο, so no alternative reading), εἰρύσσαισθε (aor. opt. mid. 2 pl., with ἄν), κυδαλίμω (nom. dual with ἀνέρε), λύοντο (impf. mid.), πέπτατο (plpf. pass. of πετάννυμι), πεπύσθην (3 dual plpf.), πληγεῖσ (aor. pass. part. fem. nom., agrees with κόρυς), ἀγχιστῖνοι (entry says sense inferred; matches note and table), ἱπποθόῳ, περιβάντα, ἔρχατο, ἔχοντο, all other novel entries: parse and meaning agree with the line and the edited `l`/`i`. All 61 novel forms covered; every `__broaden__` entry contains the old entry whole; no entry has a line number, a straight apostrophe or 230+ characters.
